\section[argumentar]{argumentar — to argue (with reasons), to make a case}

\label{lesson:PT-C337-argumentar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to debate, then the Portuguese for the argument.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: argumentar}
\textbf{argumentar} — \textquotedblleft{}to argue (with reasons), to make a case\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela argumentou que o bairro precisa de mais árvores.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She argued that the neighbourhood needs more trees.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Argumentar que…} — to argue that… It is about giving reasons, not about quarrelling.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{argumentar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{argūmentārī} \textquotedblleft{}to adduce proof of a thing\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), formed on \emph{argūmentum} \textquotedblleft{}proof\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{argumentar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{argumentar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{argumentar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to debate, then the Portuguese for the argument, then say \emph{argumentar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does argumentar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To argue (with reasons), to make a case\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[lógico]{lógico — logical}

\label{lesson:PT-C337-logico}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the argument, then the Portuguese for to argue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: lógico}
\textbf{lógico} — \textquotedblleft{}logical\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A tua resposta é lógica: se chove, ficamos em casa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Your answer is logical: if it rains, we stay at home.}
\end{quote}

\emph{É lógico!} — of course! Feminine \emph{lógica}; \emph{a lógica} is also the noun logic.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{lógico} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{logicus} (EtymDB), from Greek \emph{logikós} \textquotedblleft{}of speech, of reasoning\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{lógos} \textquotedblleft{}word, reason\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lógico}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lógico}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{lógico}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the argument, then the Portuguese for to argue, then say \emph{lógico} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does lógico mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Logical\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[convincente]{convincente — convincing}

\label{lesson:PT-C337-convincente}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to argue, then the Portuguese for logical.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: convincente}
\textbf{convincente} — \textquotedblleft{}convincing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Não foi uma resposta muito convincente.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It was not a very convincing answer.}
\end{quote}

The opposite is \emph{pouco convincente}. One form for both genders.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{convincente} goes back to Latin \emph{convincēns}, the present participle of \emph{convincere} \textquotedblleft{}to overcome, to prove\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short); it is a learned form beside the inherited verb \emph{convencer}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{convincente}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to argue, then the Portuguese for logical, then say \emph{convincente} again
\end{itemize}

\section[persuadir]{persuadir — to persuade}

\label{lesson:PT-C337-persuadir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for logical, then the Portuguese for convincing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: persuadir}
\textbf{persuadir} — \textquotedblleft{}to persuade\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tentei persuadir o meu pai a comprar um carro mais pequeno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I tried to persuade my father to buy a smaller car.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Persuadir alguém a fazer algo} — to persuade someone to do something.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{persuadir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{persuādēre} \textquotedblleft{}to convince, to persuade\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{per-} and \emph{suādēre} \textquotedblleft{}to advise, to urge\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[a convicção]{a convicção — the firm belief, the conviction}

\label{lesson:PT-C337-conviccao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for convincing, then the Portuguese for to persuade.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a convicção}
\textbf{a convicção} — \textquotedblleft{}the firm belief, the conviction\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ele falou com muita convicção.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He spoke with great conviction.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Com convicção} — firmly, with conviction.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{convicção} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{convictiō} \textquotedblleft{}demonstration, proof\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{convincere} \textquotedblleft{}to prove\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
